answer: The patient volume group with a statistically significant (p<0.05) COVID-19 severity difference between BCG and placebo is the **"1-50" patients-seen group** (Pearson chi-square = 6.219, df = 2, **p = 0.0446**, based on 126 COVID-19 AE events; BCG: Mild 25 / Moderate 30 / Severe 17 vs Placebo: Mild 16 / Moderate 33 / Severe 5). The other groups were not significant (51-100: p=0.166; >100: p=0.670 — the latter too sparse to be reliable, min expected cell <1). Caveat: this result is fragile — it depends on (i) using the AELLT COVID-19 definition that includes the 9 BCG-arm COVID-19 pneumonia events, and (ii) dropping rather than imputing the 44 AESEV-missing COVID rows; the small-group chi-square p-values (51-100, >100) are invalid due to expected cell counts <5 and are flagged with Fisher's exact (neither significant).
